title: Should have + past participle
body: The structure 'should have + past participle' is used to express regret or criticism regarding a past action that did not occur as expected, or to indicate a missed opportunity. In a healthtech startup environment, you use this to analyze post-mortems or failed clinical trial milestones. It implies that a different path was available but remained unchosen. A common error for Spanish speakers is using 'should have did' or 'should have do'. Remember: the modal 'should have' must always be followed by the past participle (e.g., 'should have launched', 'should have evaluated'). You should have audited the data flow earlier. Your team should have implemented the patient feedback loop before the Series A pitch. We should have integrated the EMR interoperability standards months ago.
keyPoints: Use 'should have' + past participle for past regrets.
Avoid the common error of using the base verb or simple past.
Apply this structure in project post-mortems to identify process gaps.
Focus on actionable hindsight for future curriculum design.
